components.name: value-settings
components.description: aws_access_key_id, aws_secret_access_key and aws_session_token hold values inline.

components.name: reference-settings
components.description: credential_process (an external command), source_profile and role_arn name where credentials come from.

claims.statement: The AWS CLI config and credentials files are plaintext files of sections with names in square brackets and entries of the form setting_name=value; lines can be commented out with a hash character; multiple profiles can be stored in one file; in the credentials file a profile section is named without the word profile.

sources.supports: These files are plaintext files that use the following format: ... Section names are enclosed in brackets ... All entries in a section take the general form of setting_name=value. Lines can be commented out by starting the line with a hash character (#). ... Multiple profiles and sections can be stored in the config and credentials files.

claims.statement: aws_secret_access_key is described as "the AWS secret key used as part of the credentials to authenticate the command request" and aws_session_token as required when temporary security credentials are specified manually; for both the page says they can be stored in the config file but recommends the credentials file.

sources.supports: aws_secret_access_key: Specifies the AWS secret key used as part of the credentials to authenticate the command request. Although this can be stored in the config file, we recommend that you store this in the credentials file.

aws_session_token: Specifies an AWS session token. A session token is required only if you manually specify temporary security credentials. Although this can be stored in the config file, we recommend that you store this in the credentials file.

claims.statement: credential_process "specifies an external command that the AWS CLI runs to generate or retrieve authentication credentials"; a profile that uses an IAM role pulls credentials from another profile named by source_profile.

sources.supports: credential_process: Specifies an external command that the AWS CLI runs to generate or retrieve authentication credentials to use for this command. credential_process = /opt/bin/awscreds-retriever --username susan
Profiles that use IAM roles pull credentials from another profile, and then apply IAM role permissions.

claims.statement: The page does not state whether aws_access_key_id or role_arn is confidential; the access key id is governed by the existing aws:iam-user-access-key family review and is not asserted here.

sources.supports: aws_access_key_id and role_arn are described as settings; no statement on confidentiality.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.

openQuestions.question: Whether the command-line arguments of a credential_process value can hold a secret is not covered; only the page's own example (a user name) is used.
